summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, at Sera Monastery (~1970–1987), and Gyuto Monastery (~1987–1988). He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1990–1992) and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ling Rinpoche, at Sera Monastery (~1980–1995), and Gyume Tantric College (1995). He taught at Virginia (1999–2000) and became director at Tibetzentrum Österreich in 2008.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned Geshe degrees while studying at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery, and he taught Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Geshe Wangyal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Agvan Dorjiev and at Drepung Monastery (~1921–1938). He taught at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983) and Columbia University (~1962–1972).
Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he is attested from 1991 through 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Chusang Rinpoche, and at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959). He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1968–1970).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University. He spent his career at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gheorghe Bogdan-Duică was an Indology scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, the Universities of Jena and Vienna (1885), and the University of Bucharest (~1889–1897). In 1919, he became Professor of Modern Romanian Literature at Babeș-Bolyai University.
Gherardo De Vincentiis worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Giacomo Lignana and served as an incaricato at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" in 1878.

Gherardo Gnoli specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, studying under Antonino Pagliaro at Sapienza University of Rome. He held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993), Sapienza (1993–2008), and directed Serie Orientale Roma (~1979–2012).

Ghulam Yazdani worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, graduating from Aligarh Muslim University (~1903–1905). He taught at St. Stephen's College (1907), Rajshahi College (1909), and Government College University (1913), before directing archaeology in Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Raniero Gnoli, at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981), and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985). She was an associate professor at Naples "L'Orientale" (1998–2017).

Giacomo Devoto was a linguist who studied at Pavia, Berlin, Basel, and Paris under scholars including Wackernagel and Meillet. He held professorships at the Universities of Cagliari (1927), Padua (1930), and Florence (1928, 1939).

Giacomo Lignana was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Turin and under Christian Lassen and Friedrich von Spiegel. He held professorships at Naples Federico II (1860–1870), Bologna (~1861–1863), and Sapienza (1870).
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1910–1914). He served at Kyoto University as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1935–1948), and was later professor at Rissho University and director of Indo Bunka Kenkyujo.
Giho Okada was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya and later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, later serving there as lecturer (1947) and professor (1968–1972) before teaching at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998), studying under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others. He has taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and Insight Meditation Center (~2001).
